summary: DB-014 authored the CP-104 remedy for the cross-tenant `staff_performance_metrics` RLS exposure: one additive, forward-only migration that drops the three permissive policies (`read_all_metrics`, `insert_metrics`, `update_metrics`) and creates three fail-closed tenant-scoped `staff_performance_metrics_scoped_*` policies. The authoring lane proved the behaviour on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (76 PASS / 0 FAIL) and never applied anything (CP-051). The apply, the postflight and the real-caller probes are the operator's, and they are the only thing standing between this and `staging_validated`. READ THE MEASURED CORRECTION BELOW BEFORE PROBING: the scoped SELECT policy the finding names as already existing DOES NOT EXIST on an ordered replay, and the `_write` policy's live text is not the one the finding cites. Both were proven by executing the chain's own guarded blocks at their own version positions. The preflight is what decides whether this file is right for your target.

operator_manifest.order: Apply this file ALONE, once, on top of whatever the target's migration history already reflects. Do NOT apply it as part of a chain replay, a `supabase migration up` over the whole directory, a `supabase db push --include-all`, a forced apply, or a `supabase db reset`. CP-051: migrations are applied manually, one at a time, reviewed and explicit. Nothing in this file depends on another migration being applied first, and nothing it does requires another migration to follow.
what_the_file_does: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS read_all_metrics / insert_metrics / update_metrics on public.staff_performance_metrics (three statements).

CREATE POLICY staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read (SELECT), staff_performance_metrics_scoped_insert (INSERT) and staff_performance_metrics_scoped_update (UPDATE, gated on BOTH using and with check with the identical rendered predicate), each to authenticated, each requiring: (venue_id IS NOT NULL OR event_id IS NOT NULL) AND has_entity_permission(auth.uid(), 'Venue', venue_id, <perm>) OR (event_id IS NOT NULL AND has_entity_permission(auth.uid(), 'Event', event_id, <perm>)), where <perm> is EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS for read and ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES for insert/update. Every has_entity_permission call is wrapped in (select ...) so the planner treats it as an InitPlan evaluated once per statement.
COMMENT ON POLICY on each of the three.

A DO block that RAISEs (and therefore aborts the transaction) unless: RLS is enabled on public.staff_performance_metrics; the three permissive names are gone; the three scoped policies exist on the right commands; each scoped predicate still carries BOTH its tenant-key conjunct and its permission check; the UPDATE policy's using and with check are the same rendered predicate; no policy on the table carries an unconditional USING or WITH CHECK for a command that takes one; and no policy on the table is reachable by anon or PUBLIC. It RAISEs a WARNING - not an exception - if no DELETE policy exists on the table, which is informational and does not block the apply.
Nothing else. No table, column, index, constraint, trigger or function. No data row read for update or deleted. Every existing staff_performance_metrics row is preserved.
what_it_does_not_touch: staff_performance_metrics_write (20260414120000:29-37, FOR ALL). It is a SCOPED policy, not a permissive one, and it is the ONLY policy the chain creates that covers DELETE on this table. Because RLS policies are permissive and OR, keeping it means NO committed surface can lose a row it could previously read, insert, update or delete.
No DELETE policy is added, so delete is neither widened nor narrowed.

public.event_resources and public.event_calendar_items. Same CP-104 shape, but a documented product decision inside DB-002's event-HQ surface. Dispositioned read-only and routed to DB-002; no migration was opened for them.
lib/database.types.ts. This migration changes no table, column or function, so it needs no type regeneration. The file is byte-unchanged.
operator_manifest.measured_correction_read_this_first: Two things in the original finding are wrong, and both were proven by EXECUTION rather than by reading, because reading is what produced the error. (1) THE SCOPED SELECT POLICY DOES NOT EXIST. 20250812093500_entity_rls_policies_more.sql:33-56 is the migration that writes `staff_performance_metrics_select` (EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS) and `staff_performance_metrics_write` (ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES). Its entire body sits inside `if exists (select 1 from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public' and table_name='staff_performance_metrics')`, and the table is created SIX DAYS LATER at 20250818120000:282 - the only `create table staff_performance_metrics` in the whole active chain. On a target where the chain has been replayed in order, 20250812093500 runs first, the guard is FALSE, and NEITHER policy is ever created. The DB-014 harness ran that exact block at its exact version position and it created nothing; it then ran the SAME block after the table existed and got both policies. So there is no scoped SELECT policy being 'OR'd away' - there is no scoped SELECT policy at all. (2) THE `_write` TEXT IS NOT THE ONE CITED. 20260414120000_security_linter_step3_tighten_rls.sql:26-39 runs AFTER the table exists, so its guard is true, and it drops `staff_performance_metrics_write` and re-creates it `for all` with the USING mirrored into WITH CHECK. The live scoped policy is the 20260414120000 body; the 20250812093500 text at :49-55 is historical. CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU: the three CREATE POLICY statements are not a tidy-up beside an existing scoped set, they are the ONLY read path this table will have. A caller holding just EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS had a working read before this migration ONLY because of the bug, and they have one after it because of this file. Probe 5 below exists for that reason and is the probe most likely to be skipped.
preflight_read_only_run_first: SELECT p.polname, p.polcmd, p.polpermissive, p.polroles::regrole[], pg_get_expr(p.polqual, p.polrelid) AS using_expr, pg_get_expr(p.polwithcheck, p.polrelid) AS check_expr FROM pg_policy p JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = p.polrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'staff_performance_metrics' ORDER BY p.polcmd, p.polname;

SELECT count(*) AS metric_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE venue_id IS NULL AND event_id IS NULL) AS tenantless_rows, count(DISTINCT venue_id) AS distinct_venues, count(DISTINCT event_id) AS distinct_events FROM public.staff_performance_metrics;

SELECT has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.staff_performance_metrics','select') AS can_select, has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.staff_performance_metrics','insert') AS can_insert, has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.staff_performance_metrics','update') AS can_update FROM (SELECT 1) x;
SELECT c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'staff_performance_metrics';
psql -f supabase/tests/db014_sweep_exemption_permissive_policies.sql   -- repo-wide read-only sweep-exemption detector; see HF-DB-014-SWEEP-EXEMPTION-DETECTION below
stop_conditions: STOP if a role-permissive policy is present on public.staff_performance_metrics under a DIFFERENT name than read_all_metrics / insert_metrics / update_metrics. This file does not remove it, so the exposure would survive the apply. Route it back to database; do not improvise an extra drop in the same run.

STOP if `authenticated_can_execute_has_entity_permission` is false. The three new predicates call that SECURITY DEFINER helper as the caller, so without EXECUTE they will DENY everything and the intended read path disappears. The failure direction is safe (deny, never open) but the result is a functional regression, so report it rather than accepting the apply. (This is a FUNCTION privilege, not a table grant. Unlike DB-013's staff_members policies, these three predicates contain no subquery against another table, so there is no SELECT-grant dependency to probe.)

STOP if `tenantless_rows` from the second preflight query is non-zero and the owning domain has not signed off. A row whose venue_id AND event_id are both NULL becomes invisible to EVERY caller after this migration, including a platform admin. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour and it is also a narrowing, so the number belongs in the release ticket rather than being discovered afterwards.

STOP if the apply raises. The DO block's post-condition is inside the same transaction as the change, so a raise means the target could not reach the asserted state. Capture the message; do not re-run with the post-condition removed.
operator_manifest.postflight_contract: psql -f supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope_contract.sql - expect ZERO rows of violations and exactly one summary row rendering as: DB-014 staff_performance_metrics scope|t

what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.cross_tenant_read: As an authenticated account with NO rbac_user_entity_roles row and NO override anywhere: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics;` returns 0. THE QUERY SUCCEEDS. Zero rows, NOT a permission error - the role still holds the table grant and RLS is what filters the rows. An `ERROR: permission denied for table staff_performance_metrics` here means the GRANT is missing, which is a different problem and not a pass.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.cross_tenant_sensitive_column: Same account: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE performance_rating IS NOT NULL;` returns 0. This is the probe that matches the finding. Attach it to the release ticket by name.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.cross_tenant_insert: Same account: `INSERT INTO public.staff_performance_metrics (venue_id, metric_date, performance_rating) VALUES ('<other venue uuid>', current_date, 0);` returns `ERROR: 42501: new row violates row-level security policy for table "staff_performance_metrics"`. That exact error is the correct outcome. `INSERT 0 1`, or success of any kind, is a FAILURE and means the exposure is still open.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.cross_tenant_update: Same account: `UPDATE public.staff_performance_metrics SET performance_rating = 0 WHERE id='<a row id in the other venue>';` returns `UPDATE 0`. Then `SELECT performance_rating FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE id='<that id>';` returns the original value. `UPDATE 1` is a FAILURE.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.fail_closed_tenantless_row: As ANY caller, `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE venue_id IS NULL AND event_id IS NULL;` returns 0. A row that names no tenant is invisible to everyone after this migration, including a platform admin. If the Layer 0 count of such rows was non-zero, report that number rather than treating 0 as automatically correct.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.fail_closed_on_write: As a caller who genuinely holds ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES on a venue: `INSERT INTO public.staff_performance_metrics (venue_id, event_id, metric_date, performance_rating) VALUES (NULL, NULL, current_date, 1);` returns `ERROR: 42501`. This must fail even for a legitimate caller. If it succeeds, the fail-closed rule is a permission accident rather than a rule.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.with_check_rescope: As a manager who CAN read a row: `UPDATE public.staff_performance_metrics SET venue_id='<another venue uuid>' WHERE id='<the row>';` returns `ERROR: 42501` - the row IS visible under USING, so the denial is coming from WITH CHECK. Separately, `UPDATE ... SET venue_id=NULL, event_id=NULL WHERE id='<the row>';` must also return `ERROR: 42501`; stripping a row's tenant is the case a USING-only policy would let through.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.non_regression_viewer_read: As a caller holding ONLY `EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS` on the owning venue, not `ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES`: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_performance_metrics;` returns that venue's row count, NOT 0, and their `UPDATE` and `INSERT` are both denied. THIS IS THE PROBE MOST LIKELY TO BE SKIPPED AND IT IS THE ONE THIS MIGRATION CAN BREAK. Before this file, such a caller's read existed only because of the bug; nothing in the chain had ever given them a scoped read path. If this returns 0, the apply has OVER-denied. Roll it forward with a new migration; do not accept it and do not revert this file.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.non_regression_manager_delete: As a caller holding `ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES` on the owning venue: `DELETE FROM public.staff_performance_metrics WHERE id='<a probe row>';` returns `DELETE 1`. That delete is served by the RETAINED `staff_performance_metrics_write` policy. If it returns `DELETE 0`, delete coverage was lost - that is a pre-existing property of a different migration, it is not this file's cause to fix, and it is the signal to stop and report.
what_a_correct_denial_looks_like.already_gone_is_correct: If the preflight shows the three permissive names are already absent, that is a CORRECT result, not a failed apply. Do not treat it as a reason to skip the file: the three CREATE POLICY statements are the entire change, and they are what gives this table a read path that has never existed in the chain.

what_to_attach_back: The preflight query results, captured verbatim, including the tenantless_rows count.
The apply output, including whether the post-condition DO block raised and whether it emitted the DELETE-policy WARNING.
The postflight contract output (zero violations, one summary row).
The sweep-exemption detector output (supabase/tests/db014_sweep_exemption_permissive_policies.sql), before and after.

The eight postflight probe results, each labelled with WHICH identity ran it. A denial probe run as the wrong identity is not evidence, and on this table the identities differ by permission rather than by organisation, so a probe run as the wrong one can produce a false pass.

Then set docs/engineering/migration-validation/20260926160000_staff_performance_metrics_scope_rls.json status to staging_validated and fill preflight.artifact, postflight.artifact and evidence.staging. Do not advance it to production_verified on staging evidence.

blockers: No hosted apply, no hosted probe and no hosted evidence exists, and the authoring lane could not produce any. Everything in this handoff is either static review or a local emulation on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: not Supabase, not a hosted project, not a chain replay, no `supabase db reset`, no `db push --include-all` (CP-051).

DB-002 recorded that some hosted migration versions were applied by raw Management API SQL rather than by the migration runner, so whether the three permissive policies are present on any given target cannot be answered from the chain. Only the preflight can answer it. This is the single largest reason the file is worth applying rather than declaring the finding already closed.

Whether `authenticated` actually holds EXECUTE on `public.has_entity_permission` on the hosted project is NOT verified. The chain grants it at 20260823210100:130-131 and re-grants it at 20260914090000:17, but grants are not managed uniformly across the chain. If it is absent the policies deny (safe) and the intended read path disappears (regression) - hence the preflight stop condition.

How many tenant-less rows a given target holds is unknown and decides whether the fail-closed rule reads as a clean deny or as a functional change. That is a data question only the operator's preflight can answer.
